overview.body:
**VohuManah** ​(*vohumanah*) ‌— Good ‌Mind, ​Cattle ​· ​Good ​thought — ​belongs ‌to ​the ​Zoroastrian tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is ​catalogued under ‌the ​domain ​"Good ​Mind, ​Cattle". The ​name ‌means ​"Good ‌thought".

**VohuManah** ​is ‌good ​mind, ‌cattle. ​The name ‌means ​"Good ​thought" ‌and belongs ‌to ‌the ​zoroastrian ​tradition.

PuniCodex ‌restores ​the ​name ‌as ​**VohuManah** and ​serves ‌its ​temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/vohumanah/). ​The ​restoration ​needs ‌no distinctive ‌letters ​or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form ‌would ‌lose, ‌which places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier ​2. The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form ​*vohumanah* survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in Avestan ​as ​**𐬬𐬊𐬵𐬎 𐬨𐬀𐬥𐬀𐬵**. ​Etymologically ​it means ​"Good thought".

‌The ​ASCII form ​*vohumanah* ‌survives only ​because ‌the early ​domain-name ‌system could ​not ​carry diacritics; ​it ​is a ​technological ‌compromise, not ​an ancient ‌spelling. ​The Unicode ‌restoration ​**VohuManah** recovers ‌the ​full diacritic ‌detail ​of the ​scholarly ‌transliteration directly ‌in ‌the address ​bar. ​The restoration ‌needs no ​distinctive ​letters or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form ‌would lose, ​which ‌places the ​name ​in Tier ​2.

​The letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

‌- ​**v** → ‌**V** ​— Same, ​capitalized
‌- **o** ‌→ ‌**o** — ‌Same
​- **h** ‌→ ​**h** — ​Same
​- **u** ‌→ **u** ​— ​Same
- ​**m** ‌→ **M** ​— ​Same, capitalized
​- ‌**a** → ​**a** ‌— Same
​- ‌**n** → ​**n** ‌— Same
‌- **a** ​→ ​**a** — ​Same
​- **h** ‌→ ‌**h** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/vohumanah/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**vohumanah** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​VohuManah.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"vohumanah" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"VohuManah".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"vohumanah" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"VohuManah" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌VohuManah was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​VohuManah ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌VohuManah ‌place ​good mind, ​cattle ​at the ​center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

‌### Origins ​(Myth)

‌VohuManah appears ​in ‌zoroastrian ​tradition as ​good ​mind, cattle. ​The ​name's ‌meaning, "Good ​thought", ‌shapes ​the narratives ‌told ​about this ‌figure.

​### ‌Worship and ​Memory ​(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ​VohuManah ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name ​survived into ‌the ​modern scholarly ‌record.

​The ​myths of ​VohuManah ​survive in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, ​and later ‌retellings. ​Each ​version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ‌its ‌tellers ​— poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The ‌PuniCodex entry ​does ​not ​privilege a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the ‌attestations so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌VohuManah ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is yet ​assigned ​to ‌VohuManah ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence should ​be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Zoroastrian name ​of ‌this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record is ​expected ‌to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary evidence ​remains ​the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in the ​Scholarly ​Sources ‌section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ​would ‌take ‌recognizable ​forms: votive ‌or ​dedicatory ​inscriptions ‌naming ‌𐬬𐬊𐬵𐬎 ‌𐬨𐬀𐬥𐬀𐬵, ‌sanctuary or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to ​good ‌mind and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes ​(name and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed ​against the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌VohuManah is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of good ​Mind, ‌Cattle ​in ​the ‌mind and ​to ‌ask ​what ‌of it ​endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"Good thought" ‌— ​and ‌a ​name that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​good ‌Mind, ​Cattle ​· ‌Good thought.

​Sit ‌with ​the ​restored ​form — ​VohuManah ‌— ‌and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ​become ​the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ‌a ​small ‌act ​of attention, ​a ​refusal ‌to ​let the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form ​*vohumanah* ​stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
